cards.text: The prophet Isaiah (Isaiah 1:1) just sang a song that calls the dwellers of Jerusalem and men of Judah to judge between the LORD and His vineyard (Isaiah 5:1-3). That vineyard is the house of Israel, where He looked for justice but saw bloodshed (Isaiah 5:7). Now Isaiah turns to them with woes, and friend, he's got a STACK of them.

cards.question: Isaiah's first woe is for people who keep adding house to house and field to field. How long do they keep it up?

cards.text: They end up living alone in the land. That's one guy who bought the whole street so nobody can ever borrow his ladder.

cards.question: Isaiah hears the LORD of Hosts declare that all those great mansions will be packed with people.

cards.text: Many houses will become desolate, great mansions left unoccupied. All that real estate, and NOBODY home to answer the doorbell.

cards.question: Then the LORD says ten acres of vineyard will yield but a bath of wine. What does that say about the land's harvests?

cards.text: Same with the grain: a homer of seed will yield only an ephah. I don't know about you, but 'only' is the LAST word I want to hear at harvest time.
Woe number two is for people who rise early in the morning in pursuit of strong drink and linger into the evening. They beat the alarm clock, and it is NOT to hit the gym.
Their feasts come with lyre and harp, tambourines and flutes and wine. That's not a party, friend, that's a TOUR.

cards.question: With all that music going at their feasts, what do these partiers fail to see?

answers.text: The work of the LORD's hands
The warnings of the city guards
The start of the harvest season

cards.question: Isaiah says the people will go into exile for their lack of understanding.

cards.text: Their dignitaries are starving, and their masses are parched with thirst. No more feasts.
Then Isaiah says Sheol enlarges its throat and opens wide its enormous jaws. Friend, that's a picture you don't shake off.

cards.question: Sheol opens wide its enormous jaws. Who goes down?
Mankind will be brought low, each man humbled, and the ___ will lower their eyes.
While mankind is brought low, the LORD of Hosts will be ___ by His justice.

cards.text: Lambs will graze as in their own pastures. And all those fancy places of the wealthy will end up as ruins.

cards.question: Isaiah says strangers will feed in the ruins of the wealthy.

cards.text: Woe number three is for those who draw iniquity with cords of deceit and pull sin along with cart ropes. Most folks TRIP into sin, but these folks hitch it up and haul it around like a moving trailer.

cards.question: These same rope-pullers talk about the plan of the Holy One of Israel. What do they say?

answers.text: Let Him hurry so we can see it
Let Him wait until we repent
Let Him keep it from the nations

cards.text: They want the Holy One of Israel to hurry His plan so they can see it and know it. That's some BOLD talk from folks dragging sin around on a cart rope.
The next woe is for people who flip everything upside down. They turn darkness to light and light to darkness, and they swap bitter and sweet.

cards.question: This woe is also for people who call evil good and good evil.
Isaiah's next woe is for people who are wise and clever in someone's sight. Whose?

cards.text: Wise in their own eyes? Friend, when my stamps started coming out blurry, I told everybody it was a "rustic look."
Then comes a woe for those who are heroes in drinking wine and champions in mixing strong drink. That is ONE trophy nobody should be putting on the shelf.

cards.question: These drinking champions also take bribes. For a bribe, they acquit the ___.
Meanwhile, these bribe-takers make sure the innocent get justice.

cards.text: So Isaiah says that as fire eats up straw and dry grass shrivels in the flame, their roots will decay and their blossoms will blow away like dust.

cards.question: Why does Isaiah say their roots will decay and their blossoms blow away?

answers.text: They lost a long war with Egypt
They let their fields go unplanted

cards.text: Therefore the anger of the LORD burns against His people, and His hand is raised against them to strike them down. The mountains quake, and the corpses lie like refuse in the streets.

cards.question: After all this, Isaiah says the LORD's anger has turned away.

cards.text: Then the LORD lifts a banner for the distant nations. And He has a way of calling the ones at the ends of the earth.

cards.question: How does the LORD call the nations at the ends of the earth?

cards.text: He WHISTLES, and they come speedily and swiftly. That's me when the oven timer dings.

cards.question: Coming that fast, these nations show up with loose belts and broken sandal straps.

cards.text: They're ready to go. Arrows sharpened, every bow strung, horse hooves like flint and chariot wheels like a whirlwind.
Their roaring is like that of a lion. I roared at a smoke alarm once, friend, and the smoke alarm WON.

cards.question: They growl, seize their prey and carry it away, and ___ can rescue it.

cards.text: In that day, they will roar like the roaring of the sea. Friend, you can't shush an ocean.

cards.question: In that day, if someone looks over the land, what will they see?
Isaiah says even the light will be hidden by clouds.
